key_insight: Shallow polynomial networks improve physics-informed trainability, but the hardest PDE benchmarks still require FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization.
engineering_relevance: For high-frequency or high-order PDE solvers, changing network architecture can matter more than upgrading numerical precision or optimization alone.
method: Replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions in PI-SUPNs.
Evaluate architecture, precision, and curvature-aware optimization across PDE benchmarks.
Establish quasi-local approximation properties and spline-based convergence bounds.
evidence_signal: PI-SUPNs alone recovered the high-frequency Helmholtz solution among tested architectures; higher beam modes required PI-SUPNs plus FP64 and curvature-aware optimization, while Allen–Cahn tests showed lower solution and derivative errors at reduced computational cost.
watch_item: Benchmark successes do not establish universal superiority, and challenging cases retain the computational requirements of FP64 and curvature-aware optimization.
paper_title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
